basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 13.' and it opens 'Vers. 13. Dic, obsecro, quod soror mea sis. Quaerunt quidam cur sanctus patriarcha'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 13. Dic, obsecro, quod soror mea sis. Quaerunt quidam cur sanctus patriarcha mentiri voluerit ut diceret Saram sororem suam, et non potius | hoc Deo commiserit qui et ejus vitam et illius servare poterat castitatem. In quo ostenditur quia quandiu habemus quod ex ratione faciamus, non debemus Deum tentare, sed ipsi nostrae saluti providere. Quodammodo Deum tentasset, si eam uxorem suam confessus fuisset, duas Deo res committens, suam vitam et illius castitatem. Fecit ergo pro vita quod potuit: quod vero non potuit Deo commisit, certus, si vellet, etiam apud Pharaonem ejus pudicitiam conservare posset.
